grh_fc787c97b1377baa7312.title: Baby, Baby
paragraphs: Recently separated decorator Julie is still emotionally dependent on her estranged husband Barry when she becomes involved with self-absorbed screenwriter Rick and then learns she is pregnant with Barry's child. Rick's attention fades as the pregnancy becomes more real, while Julie's friend Carol pushes her to stop measuring love by whether someone takes care of her. Julie finally confronts Rick, accepts that he is absorbed in his own career, and prepares to face motherhood without either man. Six months after giving birth to a daughter with Carol coaching her through labor, Julie meets Rick again as a more confident, independent woman and decides for herself whether he has any place in her life.

grh_fcc983d4653fcc8c4a90.title: Where Are You
paragraphs: Newlyweds Michael and his wife visit New York and suddenly discover that the Empire State Building, Times Square and eventually the entire city have been abandoned in the middle of ordinary life. With no radio broadcasts and no sign of humanity, they wonder whether mankind has been removed after exhausting divine patience with war and cruelty. Facing a silent world together, they decide that if they have been left to begin again, they must build their new life around the principle of treating others as they would wish to be treated.

grh_fc12278c235f78495308.title: The Road to Serfdom
paragraphs: A radio discussion of Friedrich Hayek's The Road to Serfdom presents his warning that centralized peacetime economic planning can concentrate power and erode individual liberty. Through staged arguments about business rules, job choice, competition, government authority and wartime regimentation, Hayek distinguishes temporary controls accepted for war from permanent controls adopted for security. He also rejects monopoly and special privilege as distortions of free enterprise. The program closes by arguing that political and economic freedom both require vigilance and that competition should be made fairer rather than replaced by central direction.
